correctness.rationale: Alternate left/right SVD singular-vector bases on path vertices simultaneously diagonalize each T and T* edge, proving N_m(T) unitarily equivalent to direct sum_i s_i J_m even with repeated and zero singular values. The Hermitian part of e^{i theta}J_m has sine eigenvalues cos(j pi/(m+1)) independent of theta; Li–Sze half-plane intersection gives all disks/empty at ordered values h_k. For K=(d-1)q+1, any i-th largest singular value times c1 appears among the first (i-1)q+1 products. Greedy peeling with multiplicities recovers all values; if the next radius is zero the remaining singulars vanish. Inputs diag(1,...,1,t) and diag(1,...,1,tprime) with 0<t<tprime<c_q/c1 have identical first (d-1)q ranges, proving optimality. I independently diagonalized real symmetric parts and recovered spectra for 36 parameter sets. This tests only bounded m,d; the SVD/Jacobi/peeling argument covers all.
